18690.title: Bimanual Interaction
18690.heading: Bimanual Interaction
18690.content:
Bimanual interaction coordinates both hands to perform a task. It may use two devices, two tracked hands, or different controls assigned to each hand.

Symmetric interaction gives both hands similar roles; asymmetric interaction gives them different but coordinated roles. Timing can also be synchronous or asynchronous. For example, one hand may establish a frame or region while the other performs a more precise action inside it.

Bimanual design can support integrated [[3D Manipulation]] and [[Progressive Refinement]], but the mapping should respect hand roles, device ergonomics, and the flow between actions rather than merely duplicating controls.

18693.title: Bin Smoothing
18693.heading: Bin Smoothing
18693.content:
Bin smoothing estimates an unknown relationship by grouping nearby predictor values and averaging their outcomes. It assumes the conditional expectation changes little within a sufficiently small neighborhood, so a constant can approximate each local segment.

Narrow bins follow local variation but contain fewer observations and produce noisy estimates; wider bins stabilize averages but can erase curvature. [[LOESS]] replaces each local constant with a more flexible local polynomial.

18696.heading: Bilinear Texture Filtering
18696.content:
Bilinear texture filtering samples the four texels surrounding a texture coordinate and blends them according to horizontal and vertical distance. The weighted average smooths magnified textures compared with [[Nearest-Neighbor Texture Filtering]].

It operates within one mip level and can blur a texture when many texels shrink into one pixel. Mipmapping addresses that minification case by supplying lower-resolution source images.

The [[Tensor Product of Modules]] represents bilinear maps universally: every bilinear map from M × N factors uniquely through a linear map from M ⊗ N.

18702.content:
Big O notation expresses an upper bound on how an algorithm's resource requirement grows for sufficiently large inputs. Writing $O(f(n))$ means that beyond some input threshold, the requirement is no more than a constant multiple of $f(n)$.

The notation emphasizes growth rather than exact machine time or small-input details. It makes complexity families such as [[Linear Time Complexity|$O(n)$]], [[Loglinear Time Complexity|$O(n\log n)$]], and [[Exponential Time Complexity|$O(a^n)$]] directly comparable.

18708.title: Bijective Function
18708.heading: Bijective Function
18708.content:
A bijective function is both injective and surjective. It pairs the elements of its domain and codomain and has an inverse function.

An operation-preserving bijection is an isomorphism, expressing that two algebraic structures have the same form.

A bijection is a one-to-one correspondence and therefore demonstrates that two sets have the same cardinality, including when both sets are infinite.

18726.heading: Bezout Identity

When the gcd is one, the identity produces modular inverses and proves coprimality consequences.

18732.heading: Bias Mitigation in AI
18732.content:
Bias mitigation in AI is the effort to identify and reduce unjust patterns in data, models, and deployment. Measures can include improving [[Dataset Representativeness]], examining labels and proxy variables, comparing outcomes across groups, changing objectives, diversifying teams, and monitoring a system after release.

No purely technical method can remove every contested value. Mitigation must begin with a definition of the relevant harm and a defensible account of fairness. It must also consider whether the application should exist at all; making a discriminatory system somewhat more balanced does not justify an illegitimate institutional use.

18735.heading: Bezout Identity for Polynomials
18735.content:
If polynomials f₁,…,fₙ over a [[Field]] are coprime, there are polynomials g₁,…,gₙ such that f₁g₁ + ··· + fₙgₙ = 1. Their generated ideal is therefore the whole polynomial ring.

The identity follows from the fact that every one-variable polynomial ideal is principal. It certifies [[Coprime Polynomials]] and supports the common-factor interpretation of a [[Polynomial Resultant]].

A Bernoulli text classification model represents each vocabulary term by whether it is present or absent in a document. For every class, training estimates a Bernoulli probability for each binary feature.

Prediction multiplies evidence from both observed and absent words under a conditional-independence assumption. This model suits tasks where occurrence matters more than repetition, but it discards distinctions between a term appearing once and appearing many times.

18750.title: Bernoulli Equation
18750.heading: Bernoulli Equation
18750.content:
For steady, incompressible, nonviscous flow along a streamline,

$$p+\frac12\rho v^2+\rho gh=\text{constant}.$$

The terms are pressure, kinetic energy per unit volume, and gravitational potential energy per unit volume. At equal height, faster flow is associated with lower static pressure, provided energy losses are negligible.

18753.content:
The Benjamini-Hochberg procedure controls the [[False Discovery Rate]] by ordering $m$ p-values and finding the largest rank whose p-value falls below its rank-scaled threshold. All p-values through that rank are selected.

The increasing boundary allows more discoveries than a uniform Bonferroni cutoff. Its guarantee holds under specified dependence conditions and concerns the repeated behavior of the full procedure, not the exact error share in one observed list.

18780.title: Bearer Token
18780.heading: Bearer Token
18780.content:
A bearer token authorizes whoever presents it, so possession of the token is sufficient for the protected server to consider the associated access claim. The stock-checker client places its token in the HTTP authorization header before calling the API.

Because the credential is usable by its bearer, it must be protected in transport and storage and limited to the intended resource and scope. The API validates it before the controller's protected operation is allowed to run.

18783.heading: Bearer Token Authorization
18783.content:
Bearer token authorization grants access to whoever presents a valid token in the HTTP `Authorization` header. The resource server validates the token rather than requiring the user's password on every request.

Because possession is sufficient, a bearer token must be protected in storage and transit. Its scope and lifetime should limit the damage if it is disclosed, and TLS prevents passive observers from reading it on the wire.

18786.title: Beam Deflection
18786.heading: Beam Deflection
18786.content:
Beam deflection is transverse displacement of the member's reference axis under loading. Its magnitude and shape depend on load placement, support conditions, elastic modulus, section moment of inertia, and span.

A finite element solution gives deflection at nodes and interpolates values within each beam element. Comparison with analytical solutions helps assess whether the mesh resolves distributed loading adequately.

18789.title: Beamforming
18789.heading: Beamforming
18789.content:
Beamforming combines signals from multiple microphones to emphasize sound arriving from a chosen direction and suppress competing directions. Differences in arrival time and level across the array provide the spatial evidence.

For [[Far-Field Speech Recognition]], beamforming can improve the target speaker's signal before feature extraction. In a [[Social Robot]], the estimated direction can also guide orientation and attention behavior.

18792.title: Beam
18792.heading: Beam
18792.content:
A beam is a structural member whose principal loading acts transverse to its longitudinal axis. Its response includes bending deflection, rotation, internal shear, and bending moment.

Beam theory reduces the three-dimensional member to a line model with cross-sectional properties. Finite element beam formulations approximate the transverse displacement field between nodes.

18795.heading: Beam Solar Radiation
18795.content: Beam radiation reaches a surface in essentially straight rays from the Sun without first being scattered by the atmosphere. Its direction can be followed by a tracking collector and focused by mirrors or lenses. This makes it the useful part for a [[Concentrating Solar Collector]], whereas a fixed [[Flat-Plate Solar Collector]] can also receive diffuse light. Incidence angle changes the beam energy per unit collecting area.

Beam shear force is an internal transverse resultant that balances applied loads along a beam. It is related to changes in bending moment and appears among the element end forces.

Finite element post-processing recovers shear from the solved nodal displacement and slope vector. Its sign and discontinuities depend on the adopted convention and concentrated loads.

Beam nodal slope is the rotation degree of freedom associated with the derivative of transverse deflection at a beam node. It accompanies nodal displacement in the bending element vector.

Including slope permits a smooth cubic interpolation of deflection inside the element. Applied nodal moments act through the rotational degree of freedom.

18804.title: Beam Element
18804.heading: Beam Element
18804.content:
A beam element connects two end nodes and represents flexural behavior along its length. In the primer's planar formulation, each node carries transverse displacement and slope.

The interpolation must represent both displacement and its derivative at the endpoints. The resulting element matrix relates nodal forces and moments to those displacement and rotation degrees of freedom.

18807.sourceSearchName: beam element stiffness matrix beam element stiffness matrix
18807.title: Beam Element Stiffness Matrix
18807.heading: Beam Element Stiffness Matrix
18807.content:
A beam element stiffness matrix relates two endpoint deflections and two endpoint slopes to corresponding shear forces and bending moments. Its coefficients scale with flexural rigidity and powers of element length.

The symmetric matrix is assembled using the global order of displacement and rotation degrees of freedom. Shorter elements increase the stiffness coefficients and allow finer representation of the deflected shape.

18809.title: Beam Bending Stress

18810.sourceSearchName: beam bending stress beam bending stress
18810.title: Beam Bending Stress
18810.heading: Beam Bending Stress
18810.content:
Beam bending stress varies across a section in proportion to bending moment and distance from the neutral axis. Its maximum magnitude occurs at the extreme fiber for the usual linear elastic beam model.

Finite element beam results supply moment values, while section geometry converts those moments into stress. Mesh resolution affects how accurately peak internal forces are located under distributed loads.

18811.title: Beam Bending Stress

18812.title: Beam Bending Moment
18812.heading: Document

18813.sourceSearchName: beam bending moment beam bending moment
18813.title: Beam Bending Moment
18813.heading: Beam Bending Moment
18813.content:
Beam bending moment is the internal couple associated with flexural deformation. Through the beam's moment-curvature relation, it depends on flexural rigidity and the curvature of the deflection field.

Element end moments are obtained from the beam stiffness relation after nodal degrees of freedom are known. Bending-moment diagrams expose critical regions and support reaction moments.

18814.title: Beam Bending Moment

18816.title: Bayesian Variable
18816.heading: Bayesian Variable
18816.content:
In Bayesian programming, a variable is a set of mutually exclusive and exhaustive propositions representing its possible values. Exactly one proposition can be true, and the set covers every value recognized by the model.

The variable is not intrinsically random. Its value is either known as evidence or represented by a probability distribution conditional on current knowledge. Choosing the variables determines what distinctions the model can express.

18819.title: Bayesian Switch
18819.heading: Bayesian Switch
18819.content:
A Bayesian switch activates or deactivates part of a probabilistic model through a variable included in the decomposition. When active, the selected coherence or conditional relationship constrains the connected variables; when inactive, that relationship no longer contributes in the same way.

Because the switch can be uncertain, inference may average over active and inactive cases instead of making a premature hard choice. This provides conditional structure inside the probability model itself.

18822.title: Bayesian Specification
18822.heading: Bayesian Specification
18822.content:
A Bayesian specification states the preliminary knowledge supplied directly by the modeler. It selects the variables, decomposes their joint distribution, and assigns a computable form to every factor in that decomposition.

These choices answer what the model discusses, how its knowledge is structured, and how each part is represented mathematically. Parameters not fixed by the specification can be learned during identification.

18825.title: Bayesian Question
18825.heading: Bayesian Question
18825.content:
A Bayesian question requests a conditional distribution from a description by partitioning its variables into searched, known, and free sets. It has the form $P(Searched \mid Known)$, with free variables marginalized out.

Instantiating the known variables with evidence yields one particular inference. Changing the partition can turn the same model from a predictive description into a diagnostic or control calculation.

18828.title: Bayesian Programming
18828.heading: Bayesian Programming
18828.content:
Bayesian programming is a methodology for constructing and using probabilistic models as executable programs. The modeler specifies variables, conditional structure, and mathematical forms, identifies remaining parameters from data, and asks a conditional probability question.

The approach separates modeling from inference algorithms. One description can support simulation, prediction, diagnosis, classification, or control depending on which variables are searched, known, and marginalized.

18831.title: Bayesian Program
18831.heading: Bayesian Program
18831.content:
A Bayesian program consists of a probabilistic description and a question. The description defines a joint distribution from specified structure and identified parameters, while the question states which conditional distribution should be computed.

Formally separating these parts prevents a particular inference direction from being built into the model. The same joint description can answer different questions by changing the roles assigned to its variables.

18833.sourceSearchName: bayesian program superposition bayesian program superposition
18833.title: Bayesian Program Superposition
18833.heading: Document

18834.sourceSearchName: bayesian program superposition bayesian program superposition
18834.title: Bayesian Program Superposition
18834.heading: Bayesian Program Superposition
18834.content:
Bayesian program superposition combines several probabilistic descriptions so their results jointly constrain a shared set of variables. Coherence relationships connect corresponding variables, and inference reconciles the contributions rather than selecting only one program.

This lets independently developed models supply complementary knowledge. The combined model must still account for dependencies among their evidence, because treating correlated contributions as independent can overstate certainty.

18835.sourceSearchName: bayesian program superposition bayesian program superposition
18835.title: Bayesian Program Superposition
18835.heading: References

18836.sourceSearchName: bayesian program subroutine bayesian program subroutine
18836.title: Bayesian Program Subroutine
18836.heading: Document

18837.sourceSearchName: bayesian program subroutine bayesian program subroutine
18837.title: Bayesian Program Subroutine
18837.heading: Bayesian Program Subroutine
18837.content:
A Bayesian program subroutine uses a question to one Bayesian program as the form of a distribution in another program's decomposition. Evaluating the outer factor triggers the inner inference for the current conditioning values.

The mechanism makes probabilistic models reusable without flattening every relationship into one hand-written joint distribution. The subroutine returns a distribution, so its uncertainty remains available to the calling model.

18838.sourceSearchName: bayesian program subroutine bayesian program subroutine
18838.title: Bayesian Program Subroutine
18838.heading: References

18839.sourceSearchName: bayesian program iteration bayesian program iteration
18839.title: Bayesian Program Iteration
18839.heading: Document

18840.sourceSearchName: bayesian program iteration bayesian program iteration
18840.title: Bayesian Program Iteration
18840.heading: Bayesian Program Iteration
18840.content:
Bayesian program iteration repeats a probabilistic substructure across an indexed collection or sequence. The repeated variables and factors can represent trials, sensors, objects, or time steps without writing each copy separately.

The iteration rule defines how one instance relates to earlier or shared variables. When adjacent steps depend on one another, the resulting structure supports recursive filtering and sequence models rather than independent repetition.

18843.title: Bayesian Parameter Estimation
18843.heading: Bayesian Parameter Estimation
18843.content:
Bayesian parameter estimation treats an unknown model parameter as a variable with its own prior distribution. Observed data updates that prior into a posterior over possible parameter values.

Keeping a distribution expresses remaining uncertainty and lets later predictions average across plausible parameters. New data can be incorporated by using the current posterior as the next prior.

18846.sourceSearchName: bayesian network structure learning bayesian network structure learning
18846.title: Bayesian Network Structure Learning
18846.heading: Bayesian Network Structure Learning
18846.content:
Bayesian network structure learning searches for a directed dependency graph that explains observed variables. The task identifies which conditional relationships belong in the decomposition in addition to estimating their parameters.

The number of possible graphs grows rapidly, so algorithms restrict the candidate family or search locally using a decomposable score. Any learned edge remains conditional on the data, assumptions, and scoring rule.

18849.sourceSearchName: bayesian network inference bayesian network inference
18849.title: Bayesian Network Inference
18849.heading: Bayesian Network Inference
18849.content:
Bayesian network inference computes the probability of unobserved variables after evidence is fixed on observed nodes. For classification, the central query is the posterior distribution of the class variable.

The graph's factorization avoids manipulating a fully enumerated joint table, but exact inference can still become expensive when dependencies create large intermediate factors. Approximate procedures trade exactness for tractability in densely connected structures.

18851.sourceSearchName: bayesian model combination ensemble bayesian model combination ensemble

18851.heading: Document

18852.sourceSearchName: bayesian model combination ensemble bayesian model combination ensemble
18852.title: Bayesian Model Combination Ensemble
18852.heading: Bayesian Model Combination Ensemble
18852.content:
A Bayesian model combination ensemble treats the weights assigned to a finite set of base classifiers as uncertain parameters and infers their posterior distribution. The hypothesis space therefore consists of combinations rather than the individual models alone.

This can represent complementary predictors that Bayesian model averaging might treat as competing explanations. The approach pays for that flexibility with a more complex inference problem over combination weights.

18853.sourceSearchName: bayesian model combination ensemble bayesian model combination ensemble

18854.sourceSearchName: bayesian network classification bayesian network classification
18854.title: Bayesian Network Classification
18854.heading: Document

18855.sourceSearchName: bayesian network classification bayesian network classification
18855.title: Bayesian Network Classification
18855.heading: Bayesian Network Classification
18855.content:
Bayesian network classification represents variables with a directed acyclic graph whose edges specify conditional dependencies. The graph factorizes the joint probability into local conditional distributions.

A class node can influence features directly or participate in a richer dependency structure than naive Bayes permits. Classification uses probabilistic inference to compare posterior class probabilities after observed evidence is entered into the network.

18858.sourceSearchName: bayesian model averaging ensemble bayesian model averaging ensemble
18858.title: Bayesian Model Averaging Ensemble
18858.heading: Bayesian Model Averaging Ensemble
18858.content:
A Bayesian model averaging ensemble approximates the Bayes-optimal prediction by combining sampled hypotheses with weights based on posterior support. Models can be generated from random training subsets when the full hypothesis space cannot be enumerated.

Predictions are averaged rather than selecting one fitted model with certainty. In practice, likelihood estimates and prior assumptions determine whether the weighting truly combines models or becomes dominated by one model favored by training error.

18860.heading: Document

18861.sourceSearchName: bayesian mixture model bayesian mixture model
18861.title: Bayesian Mixture Model
18861.heading: Bayesian Mixture Model
18861.content:
A Bayesian mixture model introduces a hidden choice variable whose values identify component models. Conditioned on one choice, the data follows the corresponding component distribution; marginalizing the choice produces a weighted sum of the components.

The weights are the probabilities assigned to the hidden variable and may themselves depend on observed inputs. Retaining the choice variable also allows model recognition by inferring which component best explains the evidence.

18864.sourceSearchName: bayesian information criterion bayesian information criterion
18864.title: Bayesian Information Criterion
18864.heading: Bayesian Information Criterion
18864.content:
The Bayesian information criterion scores a fitted model by balancing its maximum likelihood against a penalty that grows with the number of parameters and the amount of data. It discourages improved fit purchased through needless complexity.

In structure learning, the criterion permits candidate decompositions to be ranked with one numerical objective. It is an asymptotic approximation, so its score is evidence for comparison rather than a complete posterior over models.

18865.sourceSearchName: bayesian information criterion bayesian information criterion
18865.title: Bayesian Information Criterion

18867.title: Bayesian Inference
18867.heading: Bayesian Inference
18867.content:
Bayesian inference computes the probability distribution requested by a question from a probabilistic description. Known values condition the joint distribution, free variables are marginalized, and the remaining values are normalized over the searched variables.

The calculation can be applied in any direction supported by the joint model. Its difficulty depends chiefly on the size of the searched and marginalized spaces and on how effectively the decomposition exposes conditional independence.

18870.title: Bayesian Identification
18870.heading: Bayesian Identification
18870.content:
Bayesian identification supplies values or distributions for model parameters from observed data. It completes parts of a description that were structured by the specification but not numerically fixed by preliminary knowledge.

The learned result depends on the chosen variables, decomposition, forms, and dataset. Identification transforms some incompleteness into represented uncertainty; it does not remove the unmodeled influences outside the description.

18873.title: Bayesian Filter
18873.heading: Bayesian Filter
18873.content:
A Bayesian filter estimates a changing hidden state by combining a transition model with an observation model. At each step it predicts the new state from the previous posterior, then corrects that prediction with the latest observation.

This recursion compresses earlier evidence into the current belief distribution. Different assumptions about state spaces, distributions, and inference produce special cases such as Kalman and particle filters.

18875.title: Bayesian Estimator
18875.heading: Document
18875.content:
2026-09-06 21:47

Status: #baby

Tags: [[Bayesian Parameter and Structure Learning]]

18876.title: Bayesian Estimator
18876.heading: Bayesian Estimator
18876.content:
A Bayesian estimator identifies a model by calculating a posterior probability distribution over its parameters. The posterior is proportional to the data likelihood multiplied by the parameter prior.

Predictions can marginalize the parameter instead of substituting one best value. This carries identification uncertainty into later questions and supports sequential updating as observations accumulate.

18879.title: Bayesian Description
18879.heading: Bayesian Description
18879.content:
A Bayesian description is the probabilistic model used by a Bayesian program. It combines a specification expressing the modeler's preliminary knowledge with identification that supplies parameters learned from observed data.

Any valid joint probabilistic model can serve as a description. It exists independently of the question, so the same model can be conditioned and marginalized in several ways.

18882.title: Bayesian Decomposition
18882.heading: Bayesian Decomposition
18882.content:
A Bayesian decomposition expresses a joint probability distribution as a product of smaller conditional distributions. Each factor follows from a conditional-independence assumption encoded by the modeler.

The decomposition must balance three goals: reduce dimensionality enough for tractable inference, retain dependencies needed for a relevant model, and produce elementary distributions that can be specified or learned. It is an algebraic representation more general than requiring every factor to contain one child variable.

18885.title: Bayesian Classification
18885.heading: Bayesian Classification
18885.content:
Bayesian classification estimates a class variable from observed attributes by computing the posterior probability of each class. The description models how attribute values depend on the class and may include priors or dependencies among attributes.

The full posterior preserves ambiguity among classes. A later decision can choose the most probable class or use costs that distinguish different kinds of classification error.

For labeled data, the classifier combines class priors with feature likelihoods and selects the class with the largest posterior score. A naive Bayes implementation assumes conditional independence among attributes; this reduces computation but requires smoothing when an unseen feature-class combination would otherwise force a zero product.

The source presents the general Bayes decision boundary: for a given predictor vector, assign the class with the largest conditional probability. Practical learning methods approximate this unknown probability from training data rather than observing the true boundary directly.

18887.sourceSearchName: bayesian cluster ensemble bayesian cluster ensemble
18887.title: Bayesian Cluster Ensemble
18887.heading: Document

18888.sourceSearchName: bayesian cluster ensemble bayesian cluster ensemble
18888.title: Bayesian Cluster Ensemble
18888.heading: Bayesian Cluster Ensemble
18888.content:
A Bayesian cluster ensemble models observed partitions as noisy evidence about latent consensus memberships. Posterior inference can estimate the consensus together with uncertainty and reliability parameters for component clusterings.

The probabilistic framework can weight inputs differently and represent ambiguous assignments. Results depend on priors and the assumed noise process, which may not match systematic differences among algorithms or data views.

18889.title: Bayesian Cluster Ensemble

18890.sourceSearchName: bayesian conditional statement bayesian conditional statement
18890.title: Bayesian Conditional Statement
18890.heading: Document

18891.sourceSearchName: bayesian conditional statement bayesian conditional statement
18891.title: Bayesian Conditional Statement
18891.heading: Bayesian Conditional Statement
18891.content:
A Bayesian conditional statement uses a choice variable to condition which probabilistic model applies. Unlike a classical branch whose condition has one known value, the choice may itself have a probability distribution.

Marginalizing the choice makes every branch contribute in proportion to its probability. The construct therefore produces a mixture when the condition is uncertain and a single selected branch when it is known.

18894.title: Bayes Theorem
18894.heading: Bayes Theorem
18894.content:
Bayes theorem relates two conditional directions through the same joint probability:

$$P(H \mid E)=\frac{P(E \mid H)P(H)}{P(E)}.$$

The prior $P(H)$ is weighted by how likely the evidence is under the hypothesis, then normalized by the total probability of the evidence. The theorem does not create a model; its result depends on the hypotheses, distributions, and evidence already specified.

The source's disease-testing example shows why accuracy alone does not determine the probability of disease after a positive result. When prevalence is very low, false positives among the much larger unaffected population can dominate the posterior despite a highly accurate test.

18897.title: Bayer Pattern
18897.heading: Bayer Pattern
18897.content:
The Bayer pattern is a common color filter array that repeats a 2-by-2 arrangement containing one red, one blue, and two green samples. Green is sampled twice because human vision is especially sensitive to luminance detail, to which the green channel contributes strongly.

The repeating layout determines which channel values are measured and which are interpolated at every pixel. A known pattern therefore predicts a periodic structure of color correlations in ordinary camera output.

18900.title: Batch-Adjusted Linear Model
18900.heading: Batch-Adjusted Linear Model
18900.content:
A batch-adjusted linear model includes both the biological predictor of interest and one or more batch terms in its [[Design Matrix]]. The biological coefficient then compares groups while holding the recorded technical factors fixed.

This approach is more flexible than applying an unadjusted two-group test independently to every feature. It requires overlap between biological groups and batches; perfect [[Technical Confounding]] leaves their coefficients unidentifiable.

18903.title: Batch Processing
18903.heading: Batch Processing
18903.content:
Batch processing groups programs and data into queued jobs that a computer executes sequentially without direct user interaction. Operators load the input, keep the expensive machine occupied, and distribute printed results afterward.

The model is efficient for repetitive workloads such as payroll and billing. It is frustrating for program development because a small error may be discovered only after a long submit-wait-output cycle.

18905.sourceSearchName: batched event processing batched event processing
18905.title: Batched Event Processing
18905.heading: Document

18906.sourceSearchName: batched event processing batched event processing
18906.title: Batched Event Processing
18906.heading: Batched Event Processing
18906.content:
Batched event processing waits briefly to handle several arriving events together. The group amortizes scheduling, communication, and storage overhead and may let a device sleep between transmissions.

Waiting enlarges response time, so batch size and interval must reflect the application's latency requirement. Safety alerts tolerate less delay than periodic environmental summaries.

18907.sourceSearchName: batched event processing batched event processing
18907.title: Batched Event Processing
18907.heading: References

18909.title: Batch Size
18909.heading: Batch Size
18909.content:
Batch size is the amount of work grouped before it moves to the next stage or reaches integration. Smaller batches reduce speculative effort, shorten feedback, and reveal workflow or design problems before they affect a large inventory.

A batch cannot always be minimized without cost, but its size should be an explicit economic choice. In game production, smaller asset sets let teams test gameplay, quality, and production rates sooner.

18912.sourceSearchName: batch versus stream processing batch versus stream processing
18912.title: Batch versus Stream Processing
18912.heading: Batch versus Stream Processing
18912.content:
Batch processing applies an operation to a dataset whose results are not urgently required. Stream processing handles each arriving element as it enters a system, making it suitable for time-sensitive labels, alerts, or measurements. The choice changes both the unit of computation and the latency the architecture must support.

The book contrasts Hadoop's batch-oriented approach with Storm's stream-oriented approach and describes Spark and Flink as combining capabilities. The general design question is not which platform name is fashionable, but whether the task needs a historical aggregate, a prompt response to each event, or both.

18913.sourceSearchName: batch versus stream processing batch versus stream processing
18913.title: Batch versus Stream Processing

18915.title: Batch Learning
18915.heading: Batch Learning
18915.content:
Batch learning calculates model updates from a collection of training examples rather than changing weights after every single example. Grouping examples exposes parallel work and can make memory access and communication more efficient.

Batch size affects runtime, memory use, update frequency, and optimization behavior. A large batch is not automatically better if it delays useful parameter updates or exceeds local memory.

18918.title: Batch Effect
18918.heading: Batch Effect
18918.content:
A batch effect is systematic variation caused by when, where, or how samples were processed rather than by the biological condition being studied. Dates, reagent lots, instruments, operators, and laboratories can each create shared shifts among measurements.

The effect becomes especially damaging when batch membership aligns with the outcome, because technical structure can imitate a biological difference. Experimental randomization, metadata, exploratory analysis, and model-based adjustment provide complementary protection.
links: Batch Effects and Latent Factor Adjustment

18921.title: Basis
18921.heading: Basis
18921.content:
A basis is a set of linearly independent vectors that spans a [[Vector Space]]. Every vector in the space has one unique representation as a linear combination of the basis vectors.

Changing basis changes coordinate descriptions while preserving the underlying vectors and transformations. Eigenvectors can form a basis when a matrix is [[Diagonalizable Matrix|diagonalizable]].

18924.title: Basis Vector
18924.heading: Basis Vector
18924.content:
A basis vector is one of the directional axes used to express coordinates in a space. In three dimensions, right, up, and forward basis vectors define how component values map to spatial directions.

An object's orientation or a camera coordinate system can be understood through its basis. Dot products project another vector onto these axes, while a [[Cross Product]] can construct a perpendicular axis when two suitable directions are known.

18927.title: Basic Variable
18927.heading: Basic Variable
18927.content:
In a simplex tableau, basic variables correspond to columns that form an identity matrix. Their current values are read from the right-hand side when all nonbasic variables are set to zero.

Changing the basis exchanges one basic and one [[Nonbasic Variable|nonbasic variable]], moving to an adjacent basic feasible solution.

18929.sourceSearchName: basic promise fulfillment basic promise fulfillment
18929.title: Basic Promise Fulfillment
18929.heading: Document

18930.sourceSearchName: basic promise fulfillment basic promise fulfillment
18930.title: Basic Promise Fulfillment
18930.heading: Basic Promise Fulfillment
18930.content:
Basic promise fulfillment means the producer delivers the functions and qualities explicitly agreed upon. Standards-oriented engineering, testing, and disciplined development support this first level of genuine integrity.

Fulfilling promises is necessary but not sufficient for excellent design. Written commitments may omit contextual needs, future breakdowns, or opportunities that users could not articulate beforehand.

18933.title: Basic Authentication
18933.heading: Basic Authentication
18933.content:
Basic authentication places a username and password in the HTTP `Authorization` header after applying a transport-safe text encoding. The encoding is reversible and provides no cryptographic confidentiality.

The scheme is simple to implement but exposes reusable credentials whenever the transport is not protected. It should therefore be used only through an encrypted channel and with careful credential handling.

18936.heading: Base Point of a Parametrization
18936.content:
A base point of a projective parametrization is a parameter value at which every defining homogeneous polynomial vanishes. The coordinate formulas therefore fail to determine an image point there.

Base points carry algebraic and geometric multiplicities. Their contributions reduce the degree of a generically one-to-one parametrized surface from the square of the polynomial degree, linking local intersection data to global implicit geometry.

18939.title: Baseline Distribution for Cluster Validity
18939.heading: Baseline Distribution for Cluster Validity
18939.content:
A baseline distribution for cluster validity describes the index values expected when data are generated under a specified null or random model. It provides a reference for judging whether an observed clustering score is unusually strong.

When an analytic distribution is unavailable, repeated Monte Carlo trials can generate the baseline. Its meaning is conditional on the simulation assumptions and clustering method.

18942.heading: Base of a Power
18942.content:
The base of a power is the quantity repeatedly multiplied in an exponentiation. In (a^n), (a) is the base and (n) is the [[Exponent]].

The base can be a number, variable, product, or grouped expression. Its boundaries are determined by notation: in ((-2)^4), the base is (-2), while in (-2^4), the base is (2) and the negative sign is applied afterward. When the base is zero, zero and negative exponents require special care because reciprocal interpretations would involve division by zero.
